Claim_Text: In simulations, accuracy collapses with noise dimensions and subsample stability collapses alongside it, so evidence for stability-accuracy discordance rests on the real cohorts.
Theoretical_Evidence: Beyer et al. (1999) distance concentration; under isotropic Gaussian noise, pairwise Euclidean distances become uniform, destroying cluster contrast.
Empirical_Evidence: results/loop2/raw/exp1_bgss_adversarial.csv: In pure isotropic noise (d=0), ARI collapses to 0.003 and subsample stability collapses to 0.021. Fig 2a/2b.
Required_Revision: Accurate description. Maintain candid framing that synthetic isotropic simulations do not demonstrate discordance.

Claim_Text: Three of twelve methods (FCAG, FCM, FastMVC) show non-degenerate discordance on three cohorts each. Across these nine cells, mean stability is 0.684 and mean accuracy is -0.003 (permuted null ~ 0.01); across all 18 cells, the means are 0.638 and 0.046.
Theoretical_Evidence: Resampling fixed finite-sample realizations with D >> N repeatedly draws the same empirical spurious covariance or geometric outliers.
Empirical_Evidence: Table 2 in paper; 9 cells meet Rule (i') (Stab >= 0.50, Acc <= 0.05, min cluster >= 5% in >= 90% subsamples). Permuted null stability spans -0.003 to 0.049.
Required_Revision: Supported by empirical table; note that Rule (i') was post-hoc formulated after Prostate Core-Halo observation.

Claim_Text: A cohort-clustered bootstrap confirms a positive gap of +0.485 (95% CI [+0.379, +0.662]; unconstrained +0.464), showing that reproducibility does not imply correctness.
Theoretical_Evidence: Cluster-bootstrap accounts for intra-cohort correlation across resampling folds.
Empirical_Evidence: B=10,000 cohort bootstrap resamples cohorts with replacement; CI strictly excludes zero, demonstrating systematic positive gap.
Required_Revision: None; statistically sound application of cluster bootstrap.

Claim_Text: Bipartite consensus alone (0.046) and random feature gating (0.046 dense, 0.047 bipartite) match ambient consensus (0.037). BGSS raises ARI to 0.217 under bipartite consensus (+0.169 over matched random gating, 95% CI [+0.036, +0.310], Wilcoxon p = 0.031 uncorrected, n = 6), driven by Leukemia and SRBCT, but only to 0.077 under dense consensus (+0.031), where performance is confounded by a degenerate Leukemia result.
Theoretical_Evidence: Univariate filtering isolates marginal bimodality; random gating lacks SNR amplification. Dense consensus in Leukemia collapses onto an artifactual N=9-16 cluster.
Empirical_Evidence: Factorial grid: dense ambient 0.037, bipartite ambient 0.046, dense random 0.046, bipartite random 0.047, dense BGSS 0.077, bipartite BGSS 0.217. Wilcoxon p=0.031 is minimum possible for n=6.
Required_Revision: Ensure manuscript clearly states p=0.031 is uncorrected for multiple comparisons (which it currently does).

Theoretical_Evidence: Core determinacy sigma_i selects high-centrality instances, but uniform anchor sampling provides equivalent landmark coverage of the latent manifold.
Empirical_Evidence: V5 (core determinacy) 0.217 vs V4 (uniform random anchors) 0.198 -> Delta = +0.019 (95% CI [-0.040, +0.082], p = 0.84). Table 13.

Claim_Text: Bipartite compression reduces consensus-graph memory by 99.6% at N = 10^4.
Theoretical_Evidence: Dense matrix requires N(N-1)/2 floats (762.9 MB at N=10,000 in double precision); bipartite matrix requires N x L floats (3.05 MB at L=40). 3.05/762.9 = 0.4% -> 99.6% reduction.
Empirical_Evidence: tracemalloc and exact array size verification: 762.9 MB down to 3.05 MB at N=10,000.
Required_Revision: Distinguish consensus-graph auxiliary array memory (99.6%) from total process heap memory (97.4%). Manuscript already does this in Sec 6.1.

Claim_Text: Because independent runs share the same noise realization, they may repeatedly converge to the same arbitrary partition, producing high stability without correctness.
Theoretical_Evidence: In finite samples with fixed noise realization, subsampling draws from the empirical distribution P_N, preserving fixed noise correlations across subsamples.
Empirical_Evidence: Prostate and CNS cohorts: stability 0.860 and 0.549 with near-zero ARI (0.012 and 0.007). Table 2.
Required_Revision: Sound foundational premise of the paper.

Claim_Text: Bimodality-Gated Subspace Selection (BGSS): An unsupervised linear-time O(ND) feature filter that ranks dimensions via the finite-sample Bimodality Coefficient.
Theoretical_Evidence: Single-pass calculation of sample mean, variance, skewness, and kurtosis per feature across N samples: O(ND) total operations.
Empirical_Evidence: Benchmark timing shows BGSS takes <0.05s on D=15,154, N=253. Scales strictly linearly with ND.
Required_Revision: Accurate. Note Sarle (1983) attribution.

Claim_Text: Stability-Weighted Active Centroid Projection: A closed-form inductive mapping operator assigning unseen observations in O(K * |F_active|) operations using determinacy-weighted centroids in the gated feature space.
Theoretical_Evidence: Centroids are weighted averages in R^{|F_active|}. Nearest-centroid query is K Euclidean distance computations: O(K * |F_active|).
Empirical_Evidence: Table 3 and Loop 2 Exp 3 show sub-millisecond inference times.
Required_Revision: Complexity claim is correct, but the projection implicitly assumes convex, spherical cluster geometry. Fails on non-convex manifolds (ARI = -0.003 on Concentric Circles). Must state geometric limitation.

Claim_Text: Rule (i) Stab >= 0.50 and Acc <= 0.05. Rule (i') additionally requires the smallest cluster to hold at least 5% of the subsample in at least 90% of subsamples.
Theoretical_Evidence: Trivial partitions (e.g. 1 sample vs N-1) have high pairwise ARI under chance/constant assignment, falsely mimicking stability.

Claim_Text: Proposition 1 (Conditional Multimodality Separation Bound): For standard unimodal Gaussian, E[b_d] ~ 1/3 ~ 0.333. For continuous uniform, b_d = 5/9 ~ 0.556. For balanced two-component Gaussian mixture, b_d > 5/9 iff Delta/sigma_0 > 1.854.
Theoretical_Evidence: Mathematical derivation in Loop 1: For Gaussian, gamma=0, kappa=0 -> 1/3. For uniform, gamma=0, kappa=-6/5 -> 1/1.8 = 5/9. Mixture formula theta > (3+sqrt(15))/2 is mathematically exact.
Empirical_Evidence: Synthetic validation matches theoretical curve exactly (Loop 2 Exp 1).
Required_Revision: Proposition 1 implicitly implies b_d <= 5/9 is an upper bound for all unimodal distributions. In reality, b_d <= 5/9 holds ONLY for symmetric unimodal distributions. Skewed unimodal distributions (e.g. log-normal, exponential) can have b_d > 5/9! Proposition 1 must explicitly state the symmetric unimodality assumption.

Claim_Text: Proposition 2 (Exact Determinacy Identity): sum_{j=1}^N S_ij^2 = (1/M^2) sum_{m1,m2} C_{m1,m2}(pi_{m1}(i), pi_{m2}(i)), computing sample determinacy in O(M^2 N + M^2 K^2) time and O(N + K^2) working memory without materializing S.
Theoretical_Evidence: Proven algebraically in Loop 1: S_ij = (1/M) sum_m 1{pi_m(i)=pi_m(j)}. Squaring and summing over j exchanges sums into contingency tables.
Empirical_Evidence: Unit test tests/unit/test_determinacy.py verifies exact identity against dense dot-product to machine epsilon (< 1e-14).
Required_Revision: Mathematically and computationally exact. Excellent theorem/identity.

Claim_Text: Transfer-Cut spectral embedding U = B_norm D_A^{-1/2} V diag(max(1-lambda, 10^-4))^{-1/2} solves the bipartite normalized cut.
Theoretical_Evidence: Li et al. (2015) bipartite graph partitioning and Nie et al. (2024 FCAG). Transfer cut projects anchor eigensystem to sample instances.
Empirical_Evidence: Code executes transfer-cut embedding when eigensolver converges. Checked in Loop 1 and Loop 2.

Claim_Text: Theorem 1: Computational complexity of GAC pipeline is T_GAC = O(ND + D log D + M^2 N + M^2 K^2 + M I_km N |F_sub| K + M N L + N L^2 + L^3 + N L K + I_km N K^2), scaling linearly O(N) for fixed ensemble parameters, with O(NL + L^2) auxiliary memory.
Theoretical_Evidence: Derived in detail in Loop 1: BGSS is O(ND), sorting is O(D log D), determinacy is O(M^2 N + M^2 K^2), ensemble K-Means is O(M I N |F| K), bipartite construction O(MNL), W_anchor O(N L^2), eigensolver O(L^3), U embedding O(NLK), final K-Means on U is O(I_km N K^2).
Empirical_Evidence: Empirical wall-clock scaling in Table 4 and Fig 5 confirms linear scaling in N.
Required_Revision: Asymptotics are fully sound. Note that runtime power-law exponent in finite sample (N=500 to 10,000) is beta ~ 0.55-0.75 due to fixed overheads.

Claim_Text: Centroid assignment in active subspace (Eq. 9-10) avoids recomputing consensus graph upon arrival of new observations.
Theoretical_Evidence: Out-of-sample projection using active subspace centroids.

Required_Revision: Centroid nearest-neighbor projection fundamentally breaks on non-convex manifolds (e.g. Concentric Circles in Loop 2 Exp 3, ARI = -0.003). While spectral clustering separates manifold clusters in U, projecting back to Euclidean centroids destroys manifold geometry. The manuscript must acknowledge this limitation.
